protocol: Step-13 rerun of the V8 protocol on the reworked page: two fresh blind @vision reads per state on the 1440x900 final frame (one image per task; neutral filename; no source, siblings, docs or expected answer); describe first, then strict JSON. Strip protocol: two fresh blind reads per state on the weight-chart crop; strict JSON {mass_answer, top_item, nonproduction_band, action, blockers, confidence}; no scale comparison, no time/runtime inference.
candidate: Atlas v2 step 13 (progressive charts + detail rail + G visual system)
blind_input: temporary neutral copies /tmp/opencode/step13-blind/{a,w}0N.png; the committed frames keep their state names

application.description: Reads the entry (production main, src/main.c:1), 3-step path, HOTTEST tests/t.c (900 units, 3.0x) as unreached, the depth-0/1/2 chain main.c -> a.c -> b.c, and the 4-card rail; START chips name src/a.c:3 and src/main.c:4.

json.question_answered: Where is the static performance mass concentrated along the reachable production call path, and which candidate should be profiled first?

application.description: Names main.c 550 units / a.c 300 HOT / b.c 100, tests/t.c HOTTEST 900 UNREACHED, the 4-card rail with PERF-C-ALLOC-001 and PERF-C-LOOP-001, and the START chip src/a.c:3.

json.question_answered: Starting from the production entry main, which source files are reachable and where does the static cost mass (and its hottest findings) sit?

library.description: Reads ENTRY library root (no production main) at src/lib.c:1 MEDIUM, HOTTEST caller1.c 200 units 2.0x, three file cards, and the START probe src/lib.c:3.

json.question_answered: Where does execution enter this C codebase, which files are unreachable from that entry, and which file carries the most static cost?

library.description: Reads the library-root election, lib.c 100 / caller1.c 200 HOTTEST unreached / caller2.c 50, 1 of 3 reachable, 2 production unreached, and src/lib.c:3 as the start anchor.

json.question_answered: Where does static cost mass sit relative to this library's entry point, and which files never appear on any forward path from it?

no-entry.description: Reads ENTRY no entry / UNKNOWN, the NO ENTRY stub, the single UNREACHED rail card src/handler.c 100 units with PERF-C-LOOP-001, and the footer 0 of 1 reachable.

json.question_answered: Which production entry point drives the hottest static-cost path through this codebase?
json.blockers: no electable production entry; src/handler.c is UNREACHED (0 of 1 reachable)

no-entry.description: Reads no entry, the dashed NO ENTRY stub, the 1-card rail (src/handler.c, 100 units, top 100% of files), and the 0 of 1 reachable footer.

json.question_answered: Can an entry-flow map be constructed for this codebase?
json.blockers: no production entry point elected; the only file is UNREACHED

empty.description: Reads the empty state: no entry/UNKNOWN, HOTTEST no file, 0 steps, the 'no source functions recorded' stub in canvas and rail, and the empty weight panel.

json.question_answered: Which entry point and call path carries the most cost in the scanned codebase, and which files dominate it?
json.blockers: no data: no entry, 0 of 0 files, canvas and rail both show the stub

empty.description: Reads the same empty state and the state-unconditional legend/footer; identifies the stub as the answer.

json.question_answered: Which functions/files form the hottest entry-point-to-cost path in the scanned codebase, and what should be inspected next?
json.blockers: the scan produced no data (0 ok / 0 failed, no entry, no hottest file)

all-test.description: Reads no entry, HOTTEST tests/test_main.c 100 units, the NO ENTRY stub, the UNREACHED rail card with PERF-C-ALLOC-001, and 1 non-production unreached.

json.question_answered: Where is the static cost concentrated in this codebase, and what production entry point leads into it?
json.blockers: no electable production entry; the only file is a non-production UNREACHED test file

all-test.description: Reads the no-production answer, the START chip tests/test_main.c:3, the rail card and the 0 of 1 reachable / 1 file demoted footer.

json.question_answered: Which production entry point should anchor the Atlas entry-flow map, and where does the static cost mass sit?
json.blockers: no electable production entry; only a demoted non-production test file exists

capped.description: Reads entry src/entry.c 10 units, depth-1 node printed 20 of 26 reachable files shown (6 aggregated), f0.c 1,000 units HOTTEST badge 1, f1.c 999 badge 2, the 12-card rail (+14 more), and src/f0.c:3.

json.question_answered: Which file along the production entry path carries the most static cost, and where is its hotspot?

capped.description: Reads the same 3-column capped graph, the aggregated depth-1 node, the 12-card rail, and names src/f0.c:3.

json.question_answered: Which files along the call flow from the production entry point (main in src/entry.c) carry the most static cost, and where is the hottest optimization candidate?

partial-parse.description: Reads entry src/main.c 120 units 2.4x HOTTEST, 2-step path to src/broken.c 50 units WARN/partial, both rail cards, and parse 1 ok / 1 partial.

json.question_answered: Where does static cost flow from the main entry point, and which file/finding should be investigated first?

partial-parse.description: Reads the 2-depth graph, the partial badge on broken.c, the one finding PERF-C-LOOP-001, and the 100% reachability footer.

json.question_answered: From the production entry point, which files does static analysis reach, in what order, and how much static cost does each carry relative to the median?

single-file.description: Reads the single ENTRY/HOTTEST/HOT node src/solo.c 42 units 1.0x, the 1-card rail with PERF-C-ALLOC-001, and src/solo.c:3.

json.question_answered: Where is the static cost mass on the entry path from main, and which file/function is the hottest starting point?

single-file.description: Reads the same single-file state, including the 1 of 1 reachable footer and the complete definition lines.

json.question_answered: Which file carries the static cost mass on the production entry path from main, and how hot is it relative to the rest of the scan?

application.description: Reads the 51.4/48.6 paired ribbon, top files main.c 30% / a.c 16% / b.c 5.4%, component src 51% across 3 files, and the dashed non-production band.

json.mass_answer: The mass sits almost evenly split, production 51.4% vs non-production 48.6%.
json.top_item: src (production component) 51% of scanned static cost - 3 files
json.action: Drill into src/main.c, the largest single production file at 30%.

application.description: Reads the same paired ribbon and ranks; separates the one non-production file.

json.top_item: src/caller1.c at 57% of scanned static cost
json.action: Focus on src/caller1.c, the single file carrying 57%.

library.description: Reads the same 100/0 split and file ranks; notes the component src 100% across 3 files.

json.mass_answer: The mass sits entirely in production, printed as production 100%.
json.top_item: src/caller1.c at 57% of scanned static cost

no-entry.description: Reads the full production bar, the single file/component winner at 100%, and the empty non-production band.

json.top_item: src/handler.c at 100% of scanned static cost

all-test.description: Reads the same 0/100 split and the top-of-panel note.

json.top_item: src component at 100% of scanned static cost - 26 files

json.top_item: src/solo.c at 100% of scanned static cost

single-file.description: Same read; component and file both at 100%.

json.mass_answer: All scanned static cost sits in production (100%); non-production 0%.

a1.criterion: The read states the question the page answers and names one concrete file/path action. Empty, all-test and no-entry return the named stub/no-production answer; capped names src/f0.c; partial-parse names src/broken.c; single-file names src/solo.c.
framing_notes: capped: the canvas is taller than the 900px fold (1398px) by design; both reads still recover entry, HOTTEST, the 20-of-26 shown / 6 aggregated depth-1 node and the src/f0.c:3 action. V8-disclosed framing exception, A2-owned.
The strip above the canvas is the first answer surface (A8 re-baselined in step 12); the canvas is the first block.
Every 100/0 or paired split matches the page's single integer-tenths split; no read invented a time unit or a runtime claim.
